title: Gas-fired solution treatment of stainless fittings with whole-batch transfer to water
summary: Suneng’s gas-fired fork-handling furnace uses a rail-mounted car to transfer the fittings and fixtures to water together. In this project, the buyer supplies both the solution-treatment tank and the trays.
seoTitle: Gas-fired solution furnace for stainless pipe fittings
seoDescription: The 2018 agreement specifies eight 450 kW burners. Check maximum charge, furnace and process temperatures, and the scope of the quench system.
coverAlt: A batch of stainless steel pipe fittings

forkReview.imageAlt: A batch of stainless steel pipe fittings
forkReview.note: The temperatures and burner arrangement are from the contract appendix. Select the actual solution-treatment temperature for the material and process.
features: Whole-batch transfer of fittings at the furnace door
Heat the fittings on a tray. After soaking, the car lifts out the parts and fixtures together and lowers them into the buyer’s solution-treatment water tank.
Furnace-side piping supplied with the equipment
Suneng supplies the furnace-side natural-gas piping, valves, air ducts and fan. The combustion system has 8 burners rated at 450 kW each.

stages.title: Load on the tray
stages.note: Charge the stainless fittings as a batch on the tray.

stages.title: Heat with natural gas
stages.note: The gas, combustion-air and burner systems heat and soak the charge to the process requirements.

stages.title: Withdraw with the fork car
stages.note: The forks support the parts and fixtures and carry them out together.

stages.title: Immerse the batch
stages.note: Lower the workpieces and fixtures into the buyer’s water tank together.

cards.title: Supply responsibilities
definitions: Provides foundation design, furnace and drives, gas and air systems, installation and commissioning.
Supplies the quench tank, trays and fixture blocks, constructs foundations and embedded items, and provides the cable to the low-voltage distribution cabinet.

cards.title: Scope of supply
paragraphs: Supplier’s scope includes the furnace, door lift, fork car and drive, sealing system and operating platform, gas piping and valves, combustion air, burners, electrical controls and equipment documentation.

cards.title: Acceptance procedure
definitions: Once the equipment is manufactured, the supplier invites the buyer to the works to inspect fabrication, assembly and associated equipment.
Install and commission once the site is ready, then check the technical parameters under load. Acceptance is against the contract specifications.

figure.alt: Gas-fired solution treatment for pipe fittings
figure.caption: Place the pipe fittings on the tray. The gas-fired furnace heats and soaks the batch. The fork car carries parts and fixtures out together, then lowers them into the buyer’s water tank. Natural gas, combustion air, burners and electrical controls. The appendix specifies eight 450 kW burners.

forkReview.faqIntro: Workpieces, gas equipment and actual consumption per tonne.
faq: Are the tank and trays ordered separately?

The buyer provides both. The contract equipment list assigns the tank to the buyer. Suneng’s engineering records confirm the buyer also supplies the trays. Suneng supplies the charging car with the furnace.
Who provides the gas piping, fan and water tank?
The technical documents assign the gas piping, valves, air duct and fan to the supplier. The buyer provides the water tank.
Does this contract give actual gas consumption per tonne of fittings?

The available records do not include metered gas and corresponding net fitting weight by batch. The related article gives the conditions for the hourly design figures and explains how to calculate consumption from matched gas and weight records.
forkReview.source: Reference: 2018 purchase contract and technical documents for the gas-fired rapid solution-treatment chamber furnace. The equipment list assigns the tank. The main parameters cover chamber dimensions, load, controls and burners. Tray responsibility follows Suneng’s engineering check.
